payload.title: Senior Customs Operations Specialist
payload.content_html:
The opportunity

We are looking for a Senior Customs Operations Specialist to join Polestar’s Global Customs team within the Quality & Logistics organization.

As Polestar continues to expand globally, Customs has become a strategic business area that supports market growth, manufacturing expansion, supply chain resilience, and operational excellence across our international operations.

This is an opportunity to join a highly visible global function working at the intersection of logistics, manufacturing, procurement, finance, commercial operations, and legal compliance. Every vehicle launch, new market entry, manufacturing footprint, and cross-border supply chain flow relies on robust customs processes that enable growth while ensuring compliance.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

This role is not simply about compliance. It is about enabling business success in an increasingly complex international trade environment.

As a Senior Customs Operations Specialist, you will support strategic initiatives ranging from vehicle launches and manufacturing expansion to customs optimization and process development. You will play an important role in ensuring efficient customs operations, supporting compliance, and contributing to business decisions that impact Polestar’s operational performance and future growth.

This role is located at: Gothenburg, Sweden.

What you’ll do

As a Senior Customs Operations Specialist, you will act as a key customs specialist supporting international trade activities across the organization. You will work closely with internal stakeholders and external customs service providers to ensure compliant, efficient, and reliable customs operations throughout the supply chain.

You will contribute to both operational and improvement-focused initiatives while helping maintain high standards of customs governance and compliance.

This includes:

  • Providing guidance on customs classification, valuation, origin determination, and import/export compliance.

  • Supporting new vehicle launches, manufacturing footprints, logistics flows, and market expansion initiatives from a customs perspective.

  • Ensuring compliance with customs regulations and trade requirements across Polestar’s global operations.

  • Identifying, assessing, and mitigating customs-related compliance, operational, and financial risks.

  • Supporting continuous improvements in customs processes, governance, and internal controls.

  • Assisting with customs audits, compliance reviews, and interactions with customs authorities.

  • Supporting the development and maintenance of customs policies, standards, and best practices.

  • Identifying opportunities for duty optimization through free trade agreements and special customs procedures.

  • Collaborating with customs brokers, logistics providers, and authorities to ensure efficient cross-border operations.

  • Delivering customs training and awareness activities across the business.

  • Monitoring regulatory developments and translating requirements into practical business solutions.

  • Supporting the continued development of Polestar’s global customs capability and long-term strategy.

Who you are

We believe you are an experienced customs professional who combines strong technical expertise with a commercial and operational mindset. You are comfortable working across organizational boundaries, collaborating with stakeholders, and translating complex regulations into practical business solutions.

You enjoy solving complex challenges, driving improvements, and making a measurable impact on business performance in an international environment.

You bring:

  • Experience within customs, international trade, trade compliance, or customs operations.

  • Good knowledge of customs regulations, customs valuation, tariff classification, origin determination, and import/export requirements.

  • Experience supporting international supply chains and cross-border operations.

  • Experience working with customs authorities, customs brokers, and logistics service providers.

  • Understanding of customs risk management and compliance frameworks.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

  • Fluency in English, written and spoken.

In addition you:

Have experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • Automotive industry.

  • Manufacturing operations.

  • Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) programmes.

  • Customs audits and governmental reviews.

  • Multi-regional customs operations.

  • Free Trade Agreements and customs optimization programmes.

  • Export control regulations, sanctions screening, and broader trade compliance programmes.

People at Polestar

We know that change is needed. We also know that each one of us can help bring about that change. Our commitment to becoming climate-neutral by 2040 is just as important to us as being inclusive, diverse, and innovative. Together, we are creating, collaborating, and experimenting to usher in a new era of sustainable mobility.

We are an electric performance brand, determined to improve the society we live in.

Is this you?

If you are interested in joining the Polestar team, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We apply continuous selection and may close the application process once a suitable candidate has been identified.

To support a fair, objective, and competency-based selection process, candidates will complete work-related psychometric assessments as part of the recruitment journey.

Are you ready for the journey? Which is electric, by the way…

payload.title: Team Lead, Group Consolidation
payload.content_html:
The opportunity

We’re currently looking for a Team Lead, Group Consolidation to join our Group Accounting team in Gothenburg. In this role, you will be responsible for the consolidation of global financial reporting and for providing accurate, timely and uniform consolidated financial data for Polestar Group. You will lead the group closing and reporting process, act as a trusted advisor in matters related to accounting and reporting, and play a key role in the delivery of consolidated reporting and SEC filings to Nasdaq in New York.

As a people manager, you will lead a team of five and balance operational excellence with coaching and collaboration in a global finance environment.

This position is based in Gothenburg, Sweden. We believe in a hybrid way of working that supports both focused individual work and in person collaboration, enabling teams to perform at their best.

The responsibilities

In this role, you will be expected to lead and secure accurate and timely group closings and reporting at consolidated level. Working as part of Group Accounting, you will be instrumental in ensuring high quality financial reporting and analysis across the group.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading the monthly, quarterly and yearly group closing process, including group consolidation and internal and external financial reporting

  • Performing financial analysis on group level

  • Preparing external IFRS quarterly and annual financial reports

  • Providing accounting guidance to the wider finance organisation

  • Participating in finance related projects and initiatives

The ideal candidate

To succeed in this role and at Polestar, you need to be confident in navigating complex accounting topics, comfortable working under tight deadlines, and able to combine leadership with hands on expertise. You have experience taking a leading role in a team setting and are used to collaborating across functions and with external stakeholders. You communicate clearly, can provide guidance when needed, and are comfortable acting as a speaking partner on accounting and reporting matters in an international environment.

In addition, you’ll need the following qualifications:

  • A university degree in Business Administration with a focus on finance or accounting, which provides the technical foundation required for group accounting and consolidation work

  • Minimum ten years of relevant experience from a global corporate accounting function or audit environment, enabling you to manage complex group reporting requirements

  • Strong knowledge of IFRS accounting standards and group consolidation, essential for accurate external and internal reporting

  • Experience from leading or coaching a team, which is required to succeed as a people manager

  • Solid experience working with consolidation systems, primarily AARO, used in the group consolidation process

English is the language of written and spoken communication at Polestar. We are an international company with a strong growth mindset, operating in a fast moving environment where change is common and progress is continuous.

The process

If this sounds like a match for your ambitions, we look forward to hearing from you. We apply continuous selection and may close the application process once a suitable candidate has been identified.

As part of our recruitment process, you will complete work-related psychometric assessments. These assessments are designed to support an objective and fair evaluation of the competencies, skills, and potential required for success in the role.

Are you ready for the journey? Which is electric, by the way...

payload.title: Product Cybersecurity Engineer
payload.content_html:
The opportunity

We're looking for a Product Cybersecurity Engineer to help ensure that Polestar's products meet global cybersecurity standards and regulatory requirements throughout the vehicle lifecycle. In this role, you will work across concept, development, production, and post-launch operations, contributing to the implementation and validation of cybersecurity requirements that help safeguard our vehicle systems.

Let us describe the challenge we offer

As a Product Cybersecurity Engineer, you will play a key role in defining, integrating, and verifying technical security controls across our products. Working closely with R&D, suppliers, and cross-functional teams, you will support secure product development through threat analysis, secure design, cybersecurity validation, and regulatory compliance activities.

This role is located at our HQ in Gothenburg, Sweden.

What you'll do

You will be responsible for implementing and validating cybersecurity requirements across the vehicle lifecycle while supporting compliance with standards and regulations such as ISO/SAE 21434 and UNECE R155.

This includes:

  • Define, decompose, trace, and maintain product cybersecurity requirements and assurance cases.

  • Perform and/or support Threat Analysis and Risk Assessments (TARA) and risk treatment activities.

  • Plan and execute cybersecurity validation and verification activities, including testing and reviews.

  • Review supplier cybersecurity work products and support the closure of identified findings.

  • Support the generation of technical evidence required for regulatory audits and type approvals.

  • Collaborate with system architects, software and hardware teams, and functional safety teams to ensure secure integration.

  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of security engineering methods, tools, and templates.

Who you are

You are an experienced cybersecurity engineer with a strong background in product or embedded cybersecurity. You enjoy working collaboratively across disciplines and are comfortable balancing technical depth with regulatory and compliance requirements.

You bring:

  • A minimum of 5 years of experience in product or embedded cybersecurity engineering.

  • Strong knowledge of ISO/SAE 21434, UNECE R155, and secure development lifecycle practices.

  • Proficiency in TARA methodologies, security requirements engineering, and validation and verification techniques.

  • Hands-on experience with security testing tools such as CAN analyzers, fuzzers, and penetration testing frameworks.

  • A degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field.

  • Relevant cybersecurity certifications, are considered a plus.

People at Polestar

We know that change is needed. We also know that each one of us can help bring about that change. Our commitment to becoming climate-neutral by 2040 is just as important to us as being inclusive, diverse, and innovative. Together, we are creating, collaborating, and experimenting to usher in a new era of sustainable mobility.

We are an electric performance brand, determined to improve the society we live in.

Is this you?

If you are interested in joining the Polestar crew, don't wait to submit your application. As part of our recruitment process, you may be asked to complete assessments and participate in background checks relevant to the position. We apply a continuous selection process, and the job posting will remain open until the position is filled.

Are you ready for the journey? Which is electric, by the way…
